title: Fractality of the Schrödinger Density for Rough Data
abstract: The observable of the Talbot effect is the intensity behind the grating: the density of the evolving field, not the field itself. Its fractality was previously known only for step data with rational jumps. We prove the general case. For arbitrary real data of bounded variation with at least one jump, the density of the free Schrödinger evolution on the torus is fractal at almost every time, with graph of upper box dimension exactly three halves. Its critical Sobolev mass diverges logarithmically, at a rate given in closed form by Wiener's jump statistic of the datum and independent of the positions and phases of the jumps. The same rate is halved along time traces and doubled for the Airy flow, so the critical mass probes the dispersion relation. Transported by the rank calculus of derangetropy operators, the theory equips every probability law with a quantum carpet: Gauss-sum revivals on quantile cells at rational times, a universal fractal at almost every other. The spectral growth rate of a single measured intensity profile returns the jump content of the grating, a prediction open to test in optical and matter-wave interferometry.
summary: This theoretical paper rigorously proves that the intensity density of the free Schrödinger evolution for rough data exhibits universal fractal properties. It establishes the upper box dimension of this density to be exactly 3/2 and quantifies the logarithmic divergence of the critical Sobolev mass. The findings connect fundamental concepts of wave dynamics, fractal geometry, and spectral analysis.
main_problem: The paper determines the general fractality of the intensity (density) of the free Schrödinger evolution for rough periodic data, extending previous results limited to simple step functions.
main_result: The density's graph is proven to be fractal at almost every time, possessing an upper box dimension of exactly three halves (3/2). Furthermore, the critical Sobolev mass diverges logarithmically, with a rate determined by Wiener's jump statistic.
method: The analysis employs advanced mathematical tools including the derangetropy operator, Fourier mode expansions, and probabilistic methods like the Borel–Cantelli lemma to analyze time-averaged properties.
model_or_system: The model is the free Schrödinger evolution on the torus, applied to the observable intensity (density) derived from rough periodic data, relating to the Talbot effect in wave optics.
key_observables: The density of the evolving field (intensity, $|u|^2$), the upper box dimension of the density's graph, and the critical Sobolev mass.
important_parameters: The jump content of the initial data (Wiener's jump statistic), time $t$, and the spectral growth rate.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the initial data is real, has bounded variation, and contains at least one jump. Some results rely on conjectures regarding almost-sure upgrades of mean laws.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the general fractal nature of the density, analyzing its time-averaged properties (e.g., time-averaged carpet and divergence), and calculating the asymptotic behavior of the critical mass using spectral representations.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical insights into the scaling and fractal geometry of quantum wave packet dynamics, connecting concepts from wave propagation (Talbot effect) to rigorous fractal analysis.
